title: The reverse logarithmic Kodaira inequality and additivity
main_claim: Setup: f:(X,E)->(Y,D) is a surjective connected-fiber morphism of smooth projective reduced-SNC pairs, with Supp f^*D contained in E, and X and every boundary stratum smooth over V=Y\D. Claim: kappa(X,K_X+E) <= kappa(Y,K_Y+D) + kappa(F,K_F+E_F), with actual vanishing when either term is -infinity. Combined with logarithmic subadditivity from the companion paper (Cor 6.2), this gives additivity, which is Popa's logarithmic conjecture in this setting.

issues.location: sections/nonvanishing.tex, Lemma pseff-threshold and Lemma nonvanishing-relative (cites CP Thm 1.3, Thm 3.4, Rem 3.3)
issues.description: Uniform pseudoeffectivity and relative pseudoeffectivity rest on Campana-Paun's orbifold cotangent theorems. These are used in an orbifold tensor form with arbitrary rational coefficients in [0,1], smooth adapted covers, and a good-model fibration. The derivations as written check out: the quotient-degree bound, the tau-infimum argument, and the pushforward with the Jacobian divisor. I did not check against the source that CP's stated hypotheses match exactly, in particular the coefficient restrictions and the generic-fiber hypothesis of Thm 3.4.
issues.evidence: "We use [CP, Theorem 1.3] in its orbifold tensor form: for a smooth projective SNC pair (Z,Delta) with rational coefficients in [0,1] and K_Z+Delta pseudoeffective, every torsion-free quotient of an orbifold cotangent tensor power on an adapted cover has nonnegative degree..."

issues.location: sections/marked-periods.tex, Lemma period-descent (BBT Thm 1.1); sections/relative-iitaka.tex (FG Def 3.2/Thm 3.6)
issues.description: Descent to the quotient S needs algebraicity of the integral Lie period image (BBT). The canonical bundle formula needs b-nefness of the moduli part for a sub-lc-trivial fibration whose boundary can have negative coefficients (FG). The paper checks the FG rank condition explicitly: R <= N Z_{J'} and h^0(NZ)=1 because kappa=0. I verified that step and the discriminant bound b_A >= 1-(1-d_I)/m_I. I did not check that the cited theorems' hypotheses match against the original sources.
issues.evidence: "Thus it is an lc-trivial fibration in the precise sense of [FG, Definition 3.2]. By [FG, Theorem 3.6] ... its moduli b-divisor is b-nef."

issues.description: The equality (additivity) depends on the companion paper Orbifold-and-logarithmic-Iitaka-subadditivity, Cor 6.2. The upper inequality is proved without it, so the two papers are not circular. The sibling review of rank 129 reports the same dependency.
issues.evidence: "The additional input for equality is the logarithmic subadditivity theorem of the companion article [Foundation, Corollary 6.2]"

coverage:
I read all seven section files of build/ (introduction, reduction, geometric-vector, marked-periods, boundary-rank, relative-iitaka, nonvanishing). Most of it I checked line by line; the Lie-group parts in the middle of marked-periods got a lighter read.

Checked in detail:
- The reduction in every sign case. The very general y is chosen outside countably many base zero divisors, which requires h^0<=1. Both the base-change argument through the Iitaka fibration and the easy-addition count hold.
- Step 2 of the logarithmic Hodge vector: the subbundle injection over D'.
- Coefficient regularity at root-cover discriminants inside V, checked through semistable reduction and the weight-extension lemma (Steenbrink E_2 degeneration and constant rank).
- The zero test: s lies in m_y O_X on a reduced fiber, and (r/tau^{e/m})^m is regular.
- The point-quotient case: constant coordinates are regular sections of aL_Y and vanish at y.
- The log-metric full-mass lemma.
- Connection Ax-Schanuel dimension lemma and orbit filling.
- Boundary drop: the primitive N^k v argument and the finite-monodromy case.
- Section estimate and adjoint bigness.
- Higgs-tail curvature, the kernel inclusion, and the degree-one-root lemma: Borel fixed point and dominance give b^-_alpha E = 0.
- Initial adjoint bigness: curvature sign and regularity of T_S(-log D_0) -> J.
- Relative Iitaka construction, valuation extraction, and the exact section lattice.
- The lc-trivial rank condition and the discriminant bound.
- Orbifold transfer: the order inequality m_I ord(c)/e + ord_I(omega) + a d_I - j(1-d_I) >= 0, which uses the same minimizer I.
- The CP threshold constants (c_i, C, R, Q=C+R).
- Relative pseudoeffectivity pushforward and the twist-removal / nef-Morse arithmetic.

Not checked against the original sources: the cited theorems themselves (CP, BBT, FG, Andre, Kempf, CKS).
sibling_notes: The family 033 board had two earlier entries: Projective-Hodge-lines (rank 111) and Logarithmic-Kodaira-dimension-and-whole-fiber-variation (rank 129). Both were no_gap_found, and both rely on the same companion paper (Orbifold-log-subadditivity Cor 6.2). This paper uses that companion only for the additivity corollary; the upper inequality is proved independently. That matches the sibling finding that there is no circularity, so the board did not change my audit.
